subject.title: [Feature]: Integrate OpenSSF Best Practices & Tooling into OpenClaw

question: Which OpenSSF supply-chain controls should OpenClaw adopt now, which should be deferred or replaced by existing safeguards, and which belong to repository or organization administration outside the source tree?
rationale: The remaining controls change trusted CI execution, scanner gates, release identity and provenance, branch protection, and organization policy, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security posture or rollout order.

options.title: Split And Phase Selected Controls
options.body: Keep this umbrella open, split owner-approved slices for Scorecard or badges, SECURITY-INSIGHTS, scanner gates, release attestations, and org settings, and validate each slice on its workflow or release path.

options.title: Keep As Tracking Only
options.body: Use this issue as a standing security roadmap item and require separate maintainer-authored issues or PRs before implementation starts.

options.title: Defer OpenSSF Program
options.body: Pause the OpenSSF-specific program only if maintainers explicitly decide current SECURITY.md, Dependabot, Dependency Guard, CodeQL, provenance, and attestations are sufficient substitutes for now.

recommendation.title: Split And Phase Selected Controls
recommendation.body: Keep this umbrella open, split owner-approved slices for Scorecard or badges, SECURITY-INSIGHTS, scanner gates, release attestations, and org settings, and validate each slice on its workflow or release path.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the project lead, owns the CODEOWNERS routing rules, and already engaged on this tracker, making him the best available owner for cross-cutting security, release, and admin direction.
